text:
emma Nguyen: Hey team — customer on acme-inc reported intermittent 500s + tail latency spikes on our text-generation endpoint. They provided a request_id: 6821f3a9 and a curl they ran. Can someone pull logs?

jake Rivera: On it. Which region / model?

emma Nguyen: us-west-2, model: gpt-redwood-1. Customer says spikes around 2026-03-01T15:12:20Z (approx).

jake Rivera: running a quick search in ELK. Query I'm using: `service:redwood-api AND json.request_id:\"6821f3a9\"` — if we have structured json fields. Also trying `message:*6821f3a9*` for unstructured.

jake Rivera: no hits so far. Could be outside retention or the request_id was truncated.

emma Nguyen: Ugh. Customer insists they saw the 500 on their side and have the full raw curl. I asked them to re-run with `X-Request-Id` header added so we get it end-to-end.

alex (sre): FYI prod logs retention changed last quarter — infra keeps full request traces for 30d, but our edge/router logs are 7d. If the request hit an edge node >7d ago it may be evicted.

emma Nguyen: Timestamp they gave is ~24 days ago, so should still be in prod index. Can you try searching by client IP + time window?

jake Rivera: good call. Running `service:redwood-api AND client.ip:198.51.100.42 AND @timestamp:[2026-02-28T15:00:00 TO 2026-03-01T16:00:00]`

jake Rivera: got partial matches — see a few requests with similar latency but different request_ids. One log line shows `error: Unexpected EOF while streaming`, and mentions `kv_cache: miss` — attaching snippet: ```2026-03-01T15:12:21Z host=api-54 gen_id=7f3e2 request_id=9f8b2... level=error msg=\"stream broken: unexpected EOF\"```

emma Nguyen: That request_id isn't the one customer gave. Maybe our header was stripped or proxied. I asked customer to include `-H 'X-Request-Id: 6821f3a9'` and to paste the exact curl.

support-bot: Reminder: for debug bundle uploads use `https://redwood.tools/debug/upload` — include the full curl and any response body.

emma Nguyen: Customer just uploaded debug bundle (link: https://redwood.tools/debug/UPLOAD_ID_abc123). It contains client logs and the curl they used. Their curl actually used `--compressed` and a proxy, so header may have been overwritten.

alex (sre): Downloading bundle now. Also, try searching our router logs for the client IP and `trace_id` from the bundle. Sometimes request_id != internal trace id. Query: `index:router_logs AND json.trace_id: \"tr-0a5c\" AND client.ip:198.51.100.42`

jake Rivera: Found a matching trace_id in router logs but it shows a 502 from upstream with body `upstream connection reset`. That's consistent with the customer's 500. Looks like the worker handling the model crashed mid-stream.

emma Nguyen: OK — can we extract the worker pod name / container id and check GPU OOM or segfaults?

\alex (sre): Yes. From trace: backend-host=inf-03, container=redwood-worker-3f2. Searching infra logs for `container=redwood-worker-3f2 AND @timestamp:[2026-02-28T15:10:00 TO 2026-02-28T15:20:00]`.

\alex (sre): Found OOM event in kube events and a runtime kill: `OOMKilled` followed by a restart. That explains abrupt EOF.

emma Nguyen: Great investigation. Customer asked whether this is on us or their usage pattern.

\alex (sre): Root cause is our worker ran out of memory while decoding a very long context + large batch. We have autoscaler configured but this was a sudden spike. Action items: notify infra to check autoscale thresholds, suggest customer reduce max_tokens or enable streaming with smaller chunking, and offer a one-time credit.

emma Nguyen: I'll draft reply to customer with repro details, link to debug bundle, and suggested mitigations. Also note we couldn't find the exact request_id in prod logs (header overwritten), but traced via trace_id and client IP.

jake Rivera: Adding a note in the ticket: `Found router 502 due to backend OOM on redwood-worker-3f2 (kube OOMKilled) — trace_id tr-0a5c matches customer bundle. No exact request_id in prod logs (likely header lost at proxy).`

emma Nguyen: Thanks all — tagging infra to adjust autoscale: @alex (sre) can you open an infra issue?

alex (sre): Will do, filing INFRA-1127 with logs and pod dump.

emma Nguyen: Closing loop with customer now. :white_check_mark:
